data.title: Unrestricted Remote Desktop Between Workstations
data.summary:
Remote Desktop connections were permitted between workstations across the estate, allowing
movement from one compromised endpoint directly to another without crossing a network
boundary.
data.description:
Workstation-to-workstation connectivity is rarely required and rarely restricted. Where it
is open, an operator moves laterally through a supported, encrypted, logged-as-normal
protocol, and each new host offers whatever credentials are cached on it.

Segmentation projects usually separate workstations from servers and leave the workstation
estate flat, so the control that would prevent this is assumed to exist and does not.

Interactive logons also leave credential material in memory on the destination, so lateral
movement by this route tends to harvest further credentials as a side effect.
data.recommendation:
* Block inbound Remote Desktop between workstations at the host firewall, permitting it only
  from designated management hosts.
* Require administrative access to flow through jump hosts rather than directly from user
  endpoints.
* Alert on workstation-to-workstation Remote Desktop sessions, which should be rare enough
  to investigate individually.
data.short_recommendation: Block workstation-to-workstation RDP and route admin access via jump hosts.
